title: Battery storage proposal draws delegations and questions
subtitle: Speed limit cuts, 2024 surplus, reserve policy, strong mayor powers, business park rules and a municipal accommodation tax.
overview: Council spent much of the evening on an information report about a proposed battery energy storage facility at 6235 Guelph Street. Several delegates, including the province's electricity system operator, spoke on it. Council received the report without making a decision {{vote:m4}}. A recommendation report is expected at a later meeting, and the site plan stage is where securities and rehabilitation details would be settled.

Council endorsed lower speed limits on five road segments and more traffic calming {{vote:m5}}. It approved extra funding for the Fergus Grand Theatre washroom renovation tied to a grant {{vote:m7}}. It directed the 2024 operating surplus to the general capital reserve and asked staff to consider funding for any newly adopted parks and recreation plan {{vote:m9}}. It also adopted an updated reserve policy {{vote:m10}}.

Council agreed in principle to a municipal accommodation tax run alongside a municipal service corporation {{vote:m15}}. It also set up a web page for mayoral decisions under strong mayor powers and asked staff to report on their impacts {{vote:m14}}. A closed session was held and the mayor reported nothing coming forward from it.

decisions.detail: Council received the information report on the rezoning for the battery energy storage facility at 6235 Guelph Street, with no decision made and a recommendation report to follow.

decisions.item: Speed limit and traffic calming review
decisions.detail: Council endorsed the proposed speed limit reductions in Report IS2025-12 and directed staff to implement the speed reduction measures, with a by-law amendment to follow.
Council authorized the upstairs washroom renovation and approved $6,908.22 from the General Capital Reserve to meet the Township's 50% share of the grant application.
Council received the report, directed the $1,910,466 surplus to the General Capital reserve, and asked staff to consider funding for projects under any newly adopted parks and recreation plan.
Council adopted the updated policy, authorized the by-law, and approved the recommended reserve transfers as at December 31, 2024, posted as of January 1, 2025.
Council adopted the 2025 Business Park Pricing Policy, which allows discounts of up to 10% in certain cases such as greater required setbacks or lots that must carry drainage from neighbouring lots.
Council received the report, approved a dedicated web page for mayoral decisions and directions, and directed staff to report back on impacts to the procedure by-law, budget process and policies.
Council agreed in principle to a municipal accommodation tax and a municipal service corporation, and approved the staged implementation approach in Report CAO2025-06.

debate: On the battery storage project, delegates in support pointed to rising electricity demand, grid reliability, local jobs, safety standards and the temporary, small footprint of the site. Some councillors pressed on the company's ownership and head offices, where equipment is made, and whether council should decide how any financial benefits are used.

Councillors asked who would pay to restore the land and who carries insurance risk. Staff said the applicant would be responsible, that the legal form of securities would be worked out at site plan stage, and that the Township does not expect to need extra insurance. One councillor also asked about vibration studies, and staff said they would look into it.

On zoning, a councillor asked why the exception beyond the recommended 2% of lot area was limited to this one site. Staff said provincial guidance recommends 2%, and larger proposals would need their own site-specific zoning applications.

On the surplus and reserves, one councillor was concerned that no money is set aside for parks and recreation facilities. Staff said general reserves have helped fund such projects and that dedicated allocations are best decided during budget and asset management planning. This led to the amendment on a future parks and recreation plan.

On strong mayor powers, councillors thanked staff for the short turnaround and suggested a lobbyist register for accountability. Staff said they were working with the mayor and would assess impacts on resources and the business plan.
